title: How Much Fiber in Carrots? 1.7g per Carrot
description: Carrots: about 1.7 g of fiber per 1 medium carrot, raw (6% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in carrots?

answer.detail: fiber in 1 medium carrot, raw (61 g)

intro: Carrots rank #10 of 10 vegetables on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in carrots by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in carrots?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists carrots, raw at 2.8 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 medium carrot, raw; 61 g) therefore has about 1.7 g of fiber and 25 calories. That is 6% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 7% of a 25 g day and 4% of a 38 g day.
Carrots are an everyday vegetable with a modest amount of fiber per carrot. Their strength is convenience: they are cheap, keep for weeks, and work as a raw snack.

sections.heading: Raw sticks vs cooked carrots
paragraphs: Cooked carrots soften and pack more tightly into a cup, so a cooked cup holds more carrot and more fiber than a raw cup of sticks.
Baby carrots are regular carrots cut and peeled; their fiber per gram is similar. Carrot juice keeps little fiber.

sections.heading: How carrots compare with other vegetables
paragraphs: Of the 10 vegetables on this site, carrots rank #10 for fiber per typical serving and #8 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 6.8 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [sweet potato](/fiber-in-sweet-potato) at 3.8 g (1 medium, baked (flesh)); [baked potato](/fiber-in-potato) at 3.8 g (1 medium, baked, flesh and skin); [green beans](/fiber-in-green-beans) at 4 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), carrots are #14 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding carrots to your day
paragraphs: A cup of raw carrots with a quarter cup of hummus is an easy 6–7 g snack. Cooked carrots add fiber to soups, stews, and lentil dishes.

Example: 1 cup carrots, 1/4 cup hummus. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 7 g of fiber, with 3.6 g from the carrots. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of carrots?
faqs.a: 2.8 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Carrots, raw). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in carrots (1 cup chopped, raw)?
faqs.a: About 3.6 g, for 128 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in baby carrots?
faqs.a: About 2.8 g per 100 g raw, the same as whole carrots. Ten baby carrots weigh roughly 100 g.
Monash University lists carrots as low-FODMAP at typical servings, so they are often a comfortable choice for people with IBS.
